newsitem.title: UK: ICI shareholders back $8 bln Unilever deal.
newsitem.headline: ICI shareholders back $8 bln Unilever deal.

text.p: Shareholders in Imperial Chemical Industries Plc on Monday gave the green light to the eight billion dollar acquisition of Unilever's speciality chemicals business.
The deal, announced last month, fits ICI's strategy of moving away from bulk chemicals into higher-margin, less cyclical light chemicals.
ICI, which expects the Unilever deal to be completed next month, is buying four companies:
- National Starch, a world leader in industrial adhesives and speciality starches.
- Quest, one of the world's leading fragrance, food and flavour companies.
- Crosfield, a producer of silicates, zeolites and silicas.
The acquisition, which has met a warm reception from industry analysts, will be financed through debt.
ICI plans to gradually reduce debt levels through a three billion stg divestment programme which includes the sale of a 62.4 percent stake in ICI Australia.
The Unilever deal will provide "...ICI with a critical mass in speciality chemicals which...we had been lacking," ICI chairman Sir Ronald Hampel told shareholders at their extraordinary meeting.
He repeated that the acquisition will be fully earnings-enhancing by 1998.
